# Results — Study 125 (Ichimoku-Cloud) on real daily tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). One recipe — Ichimoku
Kinko Hyo (Hosoda) composite signal: bullish when close is above the Kumo cloud
(Senkou A/B) *and* Tenkan-sen(9) > Kijun-sen(26); bearish when close is below the
cloud and Tenkan < Kijun. Standard settings: Tenkan 9, Kijun 26, Senkou B 52,
cloud displacement 26 bars (applied with no look-ahead — the cloud at bar t uses
only data up to bar t−26). Enter at the next bar's open. Exit: symmetric ±1 ATR(20)
barriers (conservative: stop wins a bar straddling both). Run across four liquid daily
tapes. Trades pooled: **n = 412** over ~10 years. As-of **2026-06-14**.*

## The honest test — symmetric ±1 ATR, gross (cost = 0)

A direction-symmetric payoff is the only fair way to ask *"does the signal point the
right way?"* — with TP and SL equidistant, a coin earns ≈ 0.

| Arm | n | win-rate | mean (bps/trade) | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **Ichimoku composite signal** | 412 | **49.3%** | **−8.08** | **−0.94** |
| Random direction (control)    | 412 | 43.4%     | −19.94    | −2.29     |

- The signal's gross expectancy is **−8.08 bps/trade** at HAC *t* = **−0.94** —
  statistically **indistinguishable from zero** (|t| < 2).
- The signal is **+11.86 bps better than the random control**, but the control is
  itself significantly *negative* (t = −2.29). This tells us something about *where*
  Ichimoku entries fire: at moments when the market is mean-reverting, so even a random
  direction entry at the same bars is punished. The Ichimoku filter adds value vs. an
  uninformed entry at those bars, but not enough to produce a positive expected return.
- **Per-instrument**: no ticker clears |t| ≥ 2.

| Ticker | n | win-rate | mean (bps/trade) | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| SPY  |  90 | 51.1% | +3.33 | +0.25 |
| QQQ  |  96 | 49.0% | −8.03 | −0.48 |
| IWM  | 121 | 47.9% | −16.59 | −1.06 |
| AAPL | 105 | 49.5% | −8.10 | −0.35 |

## Could you trade it? — the cost sweep

At ~**10 trades/instrument/year** (= 40 pooled/year, very low turnover), the gross is
already negative so **no positive break-even cost exists**:

| round-trip cost | net mean (bps/trade) | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| 0.0 bps (gross) | −8.08 | −0.94 |
| 0.5 bps         | −8.58 | −1.00 |
| 1.0 bps         | −9.08 | −1.06 |
| 2.0 bps         | −10.08 | −1.17 |
| 5.0 bps         | −13.08 | −1.52 |

Even at zero cost the signal is a drag. Low frequency means costs are small in absolute
terms, but the gross edge is already negative — there is no "budget" to absorb them.

## Fixed-day forward returns (alternative exit)

As a robustness check, holding for a fixed number of days after the signal:

| Hold | n | win-rate | mean (bps/trade) | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 5 days  | 412 | 51.0% | −4.30 | −0.30 |
| 20 days | 412 | 52.4% | −0.04 |  0.00 |

At 20 days the drift is essentially zero (−0.04 bps, t = 0.00). The signal does not
predict any directional move at any horizon tested.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery works when there's something to find

On a deterministic synthetic daily tape (`data.synthetic_daily`), the same engine
recovers a composite-signal edge **only when bar-level momentum is planted**, confirming
the rule is a faithful trend detector and that the real tape simply has no persistent
trend structure for it to harvest:

| Planted bar AR(1) momentum | signal gross (bps/trade) | beats random control? |
|---|--:|:--:|
| 0.00 (martingale) | ≈ 0 (noise) | marginal |
| +0.10 (persistence) | positive | yes |
| −0.10 (reversion) | noise | no |

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** Gross HAC *t* = −0.94 (|t| < 2, indistinguishable from zero).
  The signal is better than an uninformed entry at the same bars (+11.86 bps over
  random control), but this only tells us that Ichimoku entry points are adverse
  timing spots — not that the filter works. No per-instrument result clears |t| = 2.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Negative gross expectancy even before costs. Low turnover
  (~10/year per instrument) means the cost drag is small, but there is no positive
  gross budget to spend. The system is net-negative at every realistic cost level.
- **Beats a coin? — PARTIAL.** The signal outperforms a random entry at the same bars
  by +11.86 bps, but both are negative. The cloud does not provide a *positive* expected
  return — it merely reduces how negative you are vs. blind entry. That is not an edge.
